tie_reference: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: TIE.
source_note: Verified Biology Form One lesson plans (Arusha Catholic Seminary). 30 lesson plans (80 min double periods, 2 per week) covering Term I (Introduction to Biology, Laboratory Apparatus & Scientific Skills, Scientific Method & Experiments, The Cell, Types of Cells, Cell Organization) and Term II (Concept & Systems of Classification, Major Groups & Binomial Nomenclature, Viruses & Kingdom Monera, Kingdoms Protoctista & Fungi, Kingdom Plantae & Angiospermophyta, Kingdom Animalia, Nutrition & Elements in Plants, Photosynthesis, Leaf Structure & Importance).

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 1: EXPLAIN BASIC BIOLOGICAL CONCEPTS AND TERMINOLOGIES
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of foundational biological concepts
lessons.specific_competence: 1.1 Explain basic biological concepts and terminologies
lessons.main_activity: Explain the concept of Biology and basic terminologies
lessons.specific_activity: Define Biology; define and give examples of basic terminologies (organism, species, habitat)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks learners to name living things they saw on the way to school.
Defines Biology; introduces key terms (organism, species, habitat) using flashcards with examples of each.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take notes; match flashcards to definitions.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides a matching/sorting activity where groups classify local plants and animals by species and habitat.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Sort examples in groups by species/habitat.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions on the terms covered.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 2: EXPLAIN THE IMPORTANCE AND INTERDISCIPLINARY RELATIONSHIPS OF BIOLOGY
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of foundational biological concepts
lessons.specific_competence: 1.1 Explain the importance and interdisciplinary relationships of Biology
lessons.main_activity: Explain the importance of Biology and its relationship with other disciplines
lessons.specific_activity: Discuss the importance of studying Biology (health, agriculture, environment, careers); relate Biology to Chemistry, Physics, Geography, and Agriculture
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps basic terminology; asks why a farmer might need to understand Biology.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Recall previous lesson; give a reason.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains the importance of Biology and its links to Chemistry, Physics, Geography, and Agriculture using the interdisciplinary chart.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct identification of at least 2 links

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Assigns groups a career picture (doctor, farmer, conservationist, lab technician) to prepare a short case study on how that career uses Biology.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Discuss in groups; prepare and present a case study.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Facilitates discussion comparing presentations; administers the Chapter 1 Review Test.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Listen to peers; complete review test.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 3: IDENTIFY LABORATORY APPARATUS AND EQUIPMENT
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of scientific processes and laboratory skills
lessons.main_activity: Identify common Biology laboratory apparatus and state their uses
lessons.specific_activity: Identify and state uses of common Biology apparatus (microscope, hand lens, forceps, Petri dish, test tubes)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Displays a microscope and asks if learners know its use.
Displays each apparatus item and explains its name, use, and safe handling.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe and record uses in notebooks.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides an apparatus identification drill where groups rotate through stations naming and demonstrating correct handling of each item.
Administers the apparatus identification test.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 4: DEMONSTRATE BASIC SCIENTIFIC SKILLS
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of scientific processes and laboratory skills
lessons.main_activity: Practice observation, measurement, recording, and specimen drawing
lessons.specific_activity: Practice careful observation, accurate measurement, systematic recording, and labelled specimen drawing using real specimens
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps apparatus names briefly; asks what makes a "good" scientific drawing.
Demonstrates the skills of observation, measurement, recording, and specimen drawing using a sample specimen.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe demonstration; take notes on skill standards.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides hands-on practice where groups observe, measure, and draw a given specimen following the demonstrated standards.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Practice all four skills with specimens in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews sample drawings and measurements against the checklist criteria.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 5: EXPLAIN THE STEPS OF THE SCIENTIFIC METHOD
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of scientific processes and laboratory skills
lessons.specific_competence: 2.2 Explain the steps of the scientific method
lessons.main_activity: Explain the scientific method
lessons.specific_activity: Describe the steps of the scientific method (observation, hypothesis, experiment, conclusion) with everyday examples
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks how a doctor figures out what is wrong with a patient.
Explains the steps of the scientific method using the chart and everyday examples.
Guides group practice writing a hypothesis and outlining an experiment for a given everyday question (e.g. "Do plants need light?").
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Write a hypothesis and outline an experiment in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Facilitates sharing of group hypotheses and gives feedback.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 6: CONDUCT SIMPLE BIOLOGICAL EXPERIMENTS
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of scientific processes and laboratory skills
lessons.main_activity: Carry out a simple biological experiment following the scientific method
lessons.specific_activity: Carry out a simple experiment (e.g. starch test on a leaf, or effect of light on plant growth) following the scientific method steps
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the scientific method steps and the hypothesis written in Period 1.
Demonstrates the starch test/light experiment step by step, following the scientific method.
Guides groups to carry out the experiment themselves and record observations and conclusions.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform experiment in groups; record results.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers the Chapter 2 Review Test.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 7: DEFINE THE CELL AND DESCRIBE CELL THEORY
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of cell structure and organization
lessons.specific_competence: 3.1 Define the cell and describe cell theory
lessons.main_activity: Explain the concept of the cell and cell theory
lessons.specific_activity: Define a cell; describe the main points of cell theory (all living things are made of cells; the cell is the basic unit of life)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks learners what they think the smallest unit of a living thing is.
Defines a cell; explains cell theory using the chart.
Guides group discussion linking cell theory to real examples (single-celled vs multicellular organisms).
Poses oral questions reviewing cell theory.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 8: IDENTIFY AND LABEL PARTS OF A GENERALIZED CELL
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of cell structure and organization
lessons.specific_competence: 3.1 Identify and label parts of a generalized cell
lessons.main_activity: Identify and label parts of a generalized cell using the microscope and diagrams
lessons.specific_activity: Identify and label the parts of a generalized cell (nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane, cell wall) using prepared slides and diagrams
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Microscope, prepared slides, cell diagram chart
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps cell theory briefly; asks what parts learners expect to see inside a cell.
Demonstrates using the microscope to view a prepared slide, pointing out and naming visible structures.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe demonstration; take notes on parts.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides groups to use the microscope themselves and label a blank cell diagram based on their observations.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Use microscope in groups; label diagrams.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews with a practical observation checklist.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 9: DISTINGUISH PLANT AND ANIMAL CELLS
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of cell structure and organization
lessons.main_activity: Compare plant and animal cells
lessons.specific_activity: Distinguish plant and animal cells based on structure (cell wall, chloroplast, vacuole) using onion and cheek cell slides
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks if a plant cell and an animal cell look the same.
Explains structural differences between plant and animal cells using the comparison chart.
Guides microscope observation of onion cells (plant) and cheek cells (animal), with comparative diagram drawing.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe slides in groups; draw comparative diagrams.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews with a T-chart evaluation comparing plant and animal cells.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 10: DISTINGUISH PROKARYOTIC AND EUKARYOTIC CELLS
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of cell structure and organization
lessons.main_activity: Compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
lessons.specific_activity: Distinguish prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells based on the presence/absence of a true nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps plant vs animal cells; asks if bacteria have the same cell structure.
Explains the key difference between prokaryotic (no true nucleus) and eukaryotic (true nucleus) cells using the comparison chart.
Guides group construction of a T-chart comparing prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, using bacteria and plant/animal cells as examples.
Administers a diagram comparison test covering all cell type distinctions from the week.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 11: EXPLAIN ORGANIZATION FROM CELL TO TISSUE TO ORGAN
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of cell structure and organization
lessons.specific_competence: 3.3 Explain organization from cell to tissue to organ
lessons.main_activity: Explain the levels of organization from cell to organ
lessons.specific_activity: Describe organization from cell → tissue → organ, with human and plant examples (e.g. muscle cells → muscle tissue → heart)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks learners to name body parts (organs) they know.
Explains the levels cell → tissue → organ with the chart, using the heart and a leaf as examples.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct sequencing of first three levels

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides pair construction of a partial sequence diagram (cell to organ) using given examples.
Poses oral questions reviewing the sequence.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 12: EXPLAIN ORGANIZATION FROM ORGAN SYSTEM TO ORGANISM
lessons.main_competence: 3.0 Demonstrate mastery of cell structure and organization
lessons.specific_competence: 3.3 Explain organization from organ system to organism
lessons.main_activity: Explain the complete levels of organization up to the organism
lessons.specific_activity: Describe organization from organ → organ system → organism, with human/plant examples; consolidate the full sequence from cell to organism
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps cell → tissue → organ; asks what other organs work with the heart.
Explains organ → organ system → organism with examples (heart + blood vessels = circulatory system).
Guides pair/group construction of the complete sequence diagram from cell to organism using human and plant examples.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Build the full sequence diagram in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers the Chapter 3 Review Test.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 13: DEFINE CLASSIFICATION AND EXPLAIN ITS REASONS
lessons.main_competence: 4.0 Demonstrate mastery of classification of living things
lessons.specific_competence: 4.1 Define classification and explain its reasons
lessons.main_activity: Explain the concept and reasons for classification
lessons.specific_activity: Define classification; explain reasons for classifying organisms (identification, study, understanding relationships)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks how learners might sort a mixed pile of objects at home.
Defines classification; explains the reasons for classifying living things.
Guides a sorting/grouping activity using specimen pictures, letting groups create their own sorting criteria first.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Sort specimens into groups; explain their criteria.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions comparing group sorting criteria.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 14: DESCRIBE ARTIFICIAL AND NATURAL CLASSIFICATION SYSTEMS
lessons.main_competence: 4.0 Demonstrate mastery of classification of living things
lessons.specific_competence: 4.1 Describe artificial and natural classification systems
lessons.main_activity: Compare artificial and natural classification systems
lessons.specific_activity: Describe artificial classification (based on convenience, e.g. size/colour) versus natural classification (based on evolutionary relationships)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps their own sorting criteria from Period 1; asks if scientists sort organisms the same way.
Explains artificial vs natural classification systems with the chart and examples.
Guides group discussion re-sorting the Period 1 specimens using natural classification criteria instead of their own.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Re-sort specimens using natural classification in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions consolidating both systems.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 15: OUTLINE THE MAJOR GROUPS OF LIVING THINGS
lessons.main_competence: 4.0 Demonstrate mastery of classification of living things
lessons.specific_competence: 4.2 Outline the major groups/kingdoms of living things
lessons.main_activity: Describe the major groups of living things
lessons.specific_activity: Outline the five kingdoms of living things (Monera, Protoctista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia) with one distinguishing feature and example of each
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks learners to name any groups they think living things fall into.
Outlines the five kingdoms using the chart, giving one feature and example of each.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct outline of the five kingdoms

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides a group classification chart activity sorting given organism cards into the correct kingdom.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Sort organism cards into kingdoms in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions reviewing kingdom features.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 16: APPLY BINOMIAL NOMENCLATURE
lessons.main_competence: 4.0 Demonstrate mastery of classification of living things
lessons.main_activity: State and apply the rules of binomial nomenclature
lessons.specific_activity: State the rules of binomial nomenclature (genus capitalized, species lowercase, italicized/underlined); apply the rules to correctly name given organisms
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the five kingdoms; asks learners if they know a scientific name for any organism (e.g. Homo sapiens).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Recall previous lesson; share known names.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: States and explains the binomial nomenclature rules with worked examples.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take notes; practice writing examples correctly.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides a naming-rules drill in pairs where learners correct improperly written scientific names and name given organisms correctly.
Administers the Chapter 4 Review Test.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 17: DESCRIBE THE STRUCTURE AND EFFECTS OF VIRUSES
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of viruses and the major groups of living things
lessons.specific_competence: 5.1 Describe the structure and effects of viruses
lessons.main_activity: Explain viruses
lessons.specific_activity: Describe the structure of a virus; explain its characteristics and effects on living organisms (e.g. common cold, influenza)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks what learners know about diseases caused by tiny organisms (e.g. flu).
Describes virus structure (protein coat, genetic material) and characteristics using diagrams and pictures.
Guides diagram drawing and group discussion on the effects of specific viral diseases learners may know.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Draw virus diagram; discuss disease effects in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions reviewing virus structure and effects.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 18: DESCRIBE KINGDOM MONERA
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of viruses and the major groups of living things
lessons.main_activity: Explain the characteristics of Kingdom Monera
lessons.specific_activity: Describe the characteristics of Kingdom Monera (bacteria) and give examples of beneficial and harmful bacteria
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps viruses briefly; asks if bacteria are the same as viruses.
Describes characteristics of Kingdom Monera using pictures, distinguishing bacteria from viruses.
Guides group discussion classifying given examples into beneficial (yoghurt-making) or harmful (disease-causing) bacteria.
Administers a short quiz on viruses and Kingdom Monera.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 19: DESCRIBE KINGDOM PROTOCTISTA
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of viruses and the major groups of living things
lessons.main_activity: Explain the characteristics of Kingdom Protoctista
lessons.specific_activity: Describe characteristics of Kingdom Protoctista with examples (Amoeba, algae) and their habitats
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Shows a picture of pond water and asks what tiny living things might be in it.
Describes Protoctista characteristics using Amoeba and algae as examples, with pictures/microscope images.
Guides microscope/picture observation of Protoctista examples and group discussion of their habitats.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe specimens in groups; discuss habitats.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions reviewing Protoctista features.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 20: DESCRIBE KINGDOM FUNGI
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of viruses and the major groups of living things
lessons.main_activity: Explain the characteristics of Kingdom Fungi
lessons.specific_activity: Describe characteristics of Kingdom Fungi with examples (mushroom, yeast, mould) and compare with Protoctista
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Shows a picture of mould on bread and asks what it is.
Describes Kingdom Fungi characteristics using mushroom, yeast, and mould as examples.
Guides construction of a comparative chart contrasting Protoctista and Fungi based on both lessons this week.
Administers a short quiz covering Protoctista and Fungi.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 21: DESCRIBE CHARACTERISTICS OF KINGDOM PLANTAE
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of viruses and the major groups of living things
lessons.main_activity: Explain the characteristics of Kingdom Plantae
lessons.specific_activity: Describe general characteristics of Kingdom Plantae (multicellular, chlorophyll-containing, cell wall present)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks what all plants around the school compound have in common.
Describes the general characteristics of Kingdom Plantae with plant specimens as examples.
Guides group observation of various plant specimens, identifying the shared characteristics discussed.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Examine specimens in groups; record shared features.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions reviewing Kingdom Plantae characteristics.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 22: CLASSIFY CLASSES OF ANGIOSPERMOPHYTA
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of viruses and the major groups of living things
lessons.main_activity: Distinguish Monocotyledonae and Dicotyledonae
lessons.specific_activity: Distinguish Monocotyledonae and Dicotyledonae classes based on leaf venation, root type, and seed structure, using field/garden examples
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Shows a maize leaf and a bean leaf; asks if they look the same.
Explains distinguishing features of monocots and dicots (leaf venation, roots, seeds) using the classification chart.
Guides plant specimen observation and comparative table construction using monocot/dicot samples brought from the school garden/field.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe specimens in groups; build comparison table.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers a specimen identification test.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 23: DESCRIBE CHARACTERISTICS OF INVERTEBRATES
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of viruses and the major groups of living things
lessons.main_activity: Explain the characteristics of invertebrates
lessons.specific_activity: Describe characteristics of invertebrates (no backbone) and classify examples into major invertebrate phyla (insects, worms, molluscs)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks learners to name animals without a backbone that they've seen (insects, worms).
Describes invertebrate characteristics and major phyla using picture charts.
Guides picture/specimen sorting where groups classify given invertebrate examples into their correct phylum.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Sort animals into groups; justify classification.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions reviewing invertebrate classification.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 24: DESCRIBE CHARACTERISTICS OF VERTEBRATES
lessons.main_competence: 5.0 Demonstrate mastery of viruses and the major groups of living things
lessons.main_activity: Explain the characteristics of vertebrates
lessons.specific_activity: Describe characteristics of vertebrates (backbone present) and classify examples into major vertebrate classes (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps invertebrates briefly; asks learners to name animals with a backbone.
Describes the five vertebrate classes and their distinguishing features using picture charts.
Guides group classification chart activity sorting vertebrate examples into their classes, followed by a group presentation summarizing invertebrates vs vertebrates.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Sort animals into classes; prepare group presentation.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers the Chapter 5 Review Test.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 25: EXPLAIN THE CONCEPT OF NUTRITION
lessons.main_competence: 6.0 Demonstrate mastery of nutrition in plants
lessons.main_activity: Explain the concept of nutrition in plants
lessons.specific_activity: Define nutrition; explain how plants obtain and use nutrients differently from animals
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks how plants "eat" since they have no mouths.
Defines nutrition; explains how plants absorb nutrients through roots and manufacture food via photosynthesis.
Guides group discussion comparing plant and animal nutrition methods using the nutrient chart.
Poses oral questions reviewing the concept of nutrition.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 26: DISTINGUISH ESSENTIAL AND NON-ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS
lessons.main_competence: 6.0 Demonstrate mastery of nutrition in plants
lessons.main_activity: Explain essential and non-essential elements and their deficiency symptoms
lessons.specific_activity: Distinguish essential and non-essential elements (macro/micro nutrients) in plants and their roles; identify deficiency symptoms
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Deficiency symptom pictures, plant nutrient chart
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Shows a picture of a yellowing plant and asks why it looks unhealthy.
Explains essential vs non-essential elements, macro/micro nutrients, and their roles in plant growth.
Guides a deficiency-symptom picture matching activity, linking symptoms (yellowing, stunted growth) to missing nutrients.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Match symptoms to deficiencies in pairs.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions consolidating nutrient roles and deficiencies.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 27: STATE THE EQUATION AND REQUIREMENTS OF PHOTOSYNTHESIS
lessons.main_competence: 6.0 Demonstrate mastery of nutrition in plants
lessons.specific_competence: 6.2 State the equation and requirements of photosynthesis
lessons.main_activity: Explain the process of photosynthesis
lessons.specific_activity: State the word and chemical equation of photosynthesis; describe its requirements (light, water, carbon dioxide, chlorophyll)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks how plants make their own food.
States the word and chemical equation of photosynthesis; explains each requirement using the equation chart.
Guides group discussion identifying where each requirement (light, water, CO2, chlorophyll) comes from in a real plant.
Administers an equation-writing test.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 28: TEST A LEAF FOR STARCH AS EVIDENCE OF PHOTOSYNTHESIS
lessons.main_competence: 6.0 Demonstrate mastery of nutrition in plants
lessons.specific_competence: 6.2 Test a leaf for starch as evidence of photosynthesis
lessons.main_activity: Carry out a leaf starch test experiment
lessons.specific_activity: Perform the iodine starch test on a leaf, following correct experimental steps, and relate the colour change result to photosynthesis
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Iodine solution, leaves, Bunsen burner/hot water bath
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the photosynthesis equation briefly; asks how one could prove a leaf has made starch.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Recall previous lesson; predict a method.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Demonstrates the starch test procedure step by step (boiling leaf, decolorizing, applying iodine).
Guides groups to carry out the starch test themselves and record the colour change observed.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform the test in groups; record results.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Leads discussion relating the result to the photosynthesis equation; reviews the week's learning.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 29: RELATE LEAF STRUCTURE TO PHOTOSYNTHESIS
lessons.main_competence: 6.0 Demonstrate mastery of nutrition in plants
lessons.main_activity: Describe internal and external leaf structure in relation to photosynthesis
lessons.specific_activity: Describe internal/external leaf structure (stomata, palisade/spongy mesophyll, chlorophyll) and relate each part's function to photosynthesis
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks why leaves are usually broad, thin, and green.
Describes internal/external leaf structures and their functions using the leaf cross-section diagram.
Guides microscope observation of leaf cross-section slides and diagram labeling in groups.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe slides in groups; label diagrams.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Poses oral questions linking leaf structure to photosynthesis function.

lessons.title: BIOLOGY FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 30: EXPLAIN THE IMPORTANCE OF PHOTOSYNTHESIS
lessons.main_competence: 6.0 Demonstrate mastery of nutrition in plants
lessons.main_activity: Explain the importance of photosynthesis to plants and other living things
lessons.specific_activity: Explain the importance of photosynthesis (food production, oxygen release, energy source for food chains) to plants and to other living things, including humans
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Biology for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps leaf structure briefly; asks what would happen if all plants disappeared.
Explains the importance of photosynthesis for plants, oxygen supply, and food chains, using the importance chart.
Guides group discussion/poster activity summarizing why photosynthesis matters to all living things, drawing on the whole chapter (nutrition, elements, equation, leaf structure).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Discuss and summarize in groups; create a simple summary poster.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers the Chapter 6 Review Test, concluding the Biology syllabus for the year.
